items.entity: design domain length x height (aspect ratio)
items.description: Sec. 2.1 points to Fig. 1 for the beam geometry; no length, height or aspect ratio appears in the text. Sec. 4 only gives the hexagon counts HNelx=120 and HNey=60. The true L:H depends on the hexagon size and orientation produced by HoneyMesher (Ref. [9] / Fig. 1). A honeycomb domain also has jagged edges, so it is only roughly a rectangle.
readings: L:H = 2:1 (e.g. 120 x 60 element units, matching the element counts)
L:H ~ 2.3:1 (regular hexagons in offset rows: ~120*sqrt(3)*a wide x ~90.5a tall)
L:H ~ 1.7:1 (regular hexagons in offset columns: ~180.5a wide x ~60*sqrt(3)*a tall)

items.entity: structured-grid equivalent of the 120 x 60 hexagonal mesh
items.description: Sec. 4 discretizes with 120 x 60 hexagonal finite elements from HoneyMesher. Hexagon shape and size and the element formulation are not given in the text. A structured quad grid cannot reproduce this mesh, and the paper does not say which quad resolution would be equivalent.
readings: 120 x 60 square bilinear Q4 elements (one quad per hexagon, 7200 elements)
Square Q4 grid matched to the adopted physical aspect ratio at the hexagon spacing (e.g. ~139 x 60 for 2.3:1)
Refined grid, e.g. 240 x 120 Q4, with the filter radius scaled to match

items.entity: concentrated point load at lower-right corner
items.description: Sec. 2.1 and the Fig. 1 caption say only 'concentrated point load at the free end' / 'applied at the lower-right corner'. The direction is shown only in Fig. 1. +y and -y give mirror-image layouts with the same compliance; a horizontal or inclined load would change the layout.

items.entity: concentrated point load at lower-right corner
items.description: No load magnitude is given anywhere (Sec. 2.1, Fig. 1 caption, Sec. 4).

items.entity: prescribed volume fraction V_f for the single-material (M=1) case
items.description: Eq. (1) and Secs. 1, 2.1 and 4 mention 'prescribed volume fractions' V_fm, but no number is given for M=1 or for any other case.

items.entity: density field used in the volume constraint
items.description: Eq. (1) writes the constraint as V(x)_m in terms of the design variables x. Sec. 2.2.1 says the filtered-and-projected x^phys feed the stiffness interpolation. The text does not say whether the volume is measured on x, the filtered x~, or x^phys.
Only normalized Young's moduli are given (Table 1: solid E=1, void 1e-9; Eq. 14). Poisson's ratio is never stated.

items.entity: 2D analysis assumption (plane stress vs plane strain)
items.description: Sec. 2.1 says only 'two-dimensional cantilever beam'. Plane stress versus plane strain is not stated; plane strain changes the effective Poisson's ratio.
The thickness of the 2D domain is not given.
Sec. 3.0.1 introduces p without a value. Sec. 4 lists only beta, eta, r_fill and the mesh, then says all parameters are 'kept same' without giving p.

Sec. 4 sets r_fill = 4 with no unit. In HoneyMesher it is presumably a distance between hexagon centroids in mesh coordinate units. How many quad elements that equals depends on the hexagon size and spacing, which the text does not give.
readings: r = 4 element widths on the quad grid
r = 4 hexagon side-length units, i.e. ~2.3 element spacings if centre spacing = sqrt(3) x side
r scaled with the mesh if a refined quad grid is used (e.g. 8 elements on 240 x 120)

items.description: Eq. (2) uses a 'filter weight W_ej' and a neighbourhood 'determined by the prescribed filter radius'. Sec. 2.2.1 calls the filter 'classical' but gives no weight function, and does not say whether distance < r or <= r.
readings: Linear cone weights W = max(0, r - d) (classical density filter)

items.description: Sec. 4 says the projection parameter 'starts with 1 and increases up to beta_max = 32'. It does not say how beta grows or when it is updated.
readings: beta doubled when the design change drops below a tolerance (e.g. 0.01)
beta raised in small steps (e.g. +1 every fixed number of iterations) up to 32

items.description: The Abstract and Sec. 1 say only that MMA is used. Move limit, asymptote parameters, MMA constants and any scaling of the objective or constraint are not given.
readings: Svanberg default mmasub parameters (asyinit 0.5, asyincr 1.2, asydecr 0.7, a0=1, a=0, c=1000, d=1)
Default parameters plus an external move limit of 0.1
Default parameters plus an external move limit of 0.2
Objective normalized (e.g. by initial compliance C0) before passing to MMA

items.description: No convergence tolerance, iteration limit, or number of iterations at beta_max is given (Sec. 4).
readings: Fixed number of iterations per beta level (e.g. 50), stopping after the beta = 32 stage

items.description: The starting values of the design variables are not given.

Table 2 does not say whether C is the raw F^T U, a normalized value, or a scaled MMA objective. By a rough beam estimate (not from the paper), a 2:1 cantilever with E=1 and a unit corner load would have a raw compliance in the tens. So the reported value suggests a non-unit load or some normalization. This matters when checking a re-run against the paper.
readings: Raw compliance F^T U with unit load and E = 1
Compliance normalized by the initial uniform-density design's compliance
Scaled objective value as passed to MMA

items.entity: settings actually used for the M=1 SIMP run
items.description: Sec. 4 says 'All the optimization parameters are kept same'. For M=1 with E1 = 1, the SIMP rule (Eq. 4) and the DMO rule (Eq. 8) are identical, so the two runs should match. Table 2 nevertheless reports C = 2.49342 (SIMP) vs 2.6527 (DMO). Some unreported setting must differ, so the parameter set behind 2.49342 is uncertain.
readings: Use the shared settings; the SIMP and DMO M=1 runs are then identical and both reported values cannot be reproduced
Assume the SIMP M=1 run used some unreported different setting (e.g. p, V_f, iteration count or beta schedule)

locator: Sec. 2.1 / Sec. 4, the cantilever beam of Fig. 1, single-material extended SIMP case
